Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 111, verse 1:

﴿Perish﴾ when the Prophet ﷺ called his people and said: "I am a warner to you of a severe punishment before you," his uncle Abu Lahab said: "Destruction to you! Is it for this that you called us?" Then "Perish" was revealed. ﴿The hands of Abu Lahab will perish﴾, meaning his whole self; he expressed it by "hands" metaphorically, because most actions are carried out by them. This sentence is an invocation. ﴿And he will perish﴾, meaning he himself will be lost; this is a statement of fact, like the saying of people: "God destroyed him," when he has already perished. When the Prophet warned him of the punishment, he said: "If what my nephew says is true, I will ransom myself from it with my wealth and my children." Then there was revealed ﴿His wealth and what he earned did not avail him﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 111, verse 2:

﴿What his wealth availed him, nor what he earned.﴾ I.e., and what he earned, i.e., his son. "What availed" (mā aghnā) means "yughnī," i.e., it is in the sense of the present tense: "what avails."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 111, verse 3:

﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame.﴾ Meaning: it will be set ablaze and kindled. So her "kunyah" (agnomen) is an outcome of the blazing of his face, in brightness and redness.

"And his wife"—a conjunction over the pronoun in "will burn" (yaslā), which was permitted by the separation through the object and its description. She is Umm Jamil. "Carrier of firewood" (ḥammālat al-ḥaṭab)—read with both the nominative and the accusative. "Firewood" means thorny plants and sa'dan (a thistle-like prickly shrub), which she would throw on the path of the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿In her neck﴾ (her neck), ﴿a rope of palm-fiber﴾ (i.e., of fibers). This clause is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to ﴿the firewood-carrier﴾, which is an attribute (naʿt) of his wife, or it is the predicate (khabar) of an implied subject (mubtadaʾ muqaddar).
